Sakura's observed request to join the group does not independently certify group permanence, broad confidence or romance.
Hasebe's study collaboration does not demonstrate that the official final academic grade improved.
Hiyori's calm questioning near Ryūen does not establish her independence from his reconnaissance or full knowledge.
The sugar insight may be based on earlier social inquiry; no extraordinary sensory capacity may be inferred.
School clearance refutes an Ichinose fraud allegation but neither identifies the mailed-letter author nor supplies her full points ledger.
Ichinose's generosity is explicitly limited by available resources and competing obligations, not universal loyalty to rivals.
Ryūen's false-answer decision is one bounded tactic; his long-term Class A goal persists and X remains anonymous to him.
Ryūen's invasive phone test targets reactions under pressure, not a genuinely comprehensive forensic search of each device.
Manabe's coerced account yields two possible witnesses and a photograph, not authenticated X identity.
Hiyori's sugar claim and appearance in Ryūen's probing is not certified as a controlled double-blind intelligence test.
The photographed victim is threatened conditionally; no new physical assault during V6 or X unmasking is recorded.
Katsuragi's regret is direct testimony and declining faction influence; no secret new alliance is proven.
Karuizawa-mediated investigation finds prior questioning about sugar, not who commissioned it or a full conspiracy.
Karuizawa deletes sensitive correspondence but control over all copies and permanent safety are not proven.
Karuizawa intentionally dumps grape juice; mastermind, cheat-sheet author, planting time and knowledge of every step remain unproven.
Sudō's reported midterm improvement also reflects easier questions and sports adjustments; avoid permanent intelligence boost.
Kushida's middle-school narrative is first-person confession acquired privately by Suzune and Kiyotaka, not the absent Manabu.
Kushida concedes the wager ahead of official scores and rejects friendship; do not script permanent reconciliation.
Popularity, blog trauma and exposure of genuine confidences are Kushida's self-account, not diagnosis or guaranteed manipulation.
Publicly helpful exam participation can conceal a private attempt to leak questions, but does not imply every classmate knew.
Finding a note in Kushida's blazer is not an adjudicated cheating conviction; Ryūen speculates on the insertion.
Kiyotaka enters a private high-risk math wager to hear Kushida's past; knowledge remains private, and future expulsion is contingent.
Joining the five-person circle creates relationships, not an irreversible personality change or dissemination of X secret.
Kiyotaka's assurance to protect Karuizawa is neither unlimited operational protection nor reciprocal romance.
Satō is the exam partner; Kiyotaka's target score is a stated strategy, not an officially reported final score.
An intentionally average public exam score is not an actual maximum academic capability measurement.
Manabu only witnesses the betting terms; Kushida's junior-high confession is not automatically acquired by him.
Satō obtains Kiyotaka's contact information and shows one-sided interest; dating or reciprocity not established.
Satō's enthusiasm and practice are not proof of a passing official examination score or romantic outcome.
Miyake's shared humanities weakness with Hasebe is local diagnostic performance, not a permanent learning deficit.
Nagumo's inauguration establishes an office and announced intended reforms, not implementation of all governance rules.
Suzune estimates a very high math score and receives Kushida's concession, not an official results document or permanent trust.
The mathematics wager has a narrow witness and private disclosure boundary; legal enforceability and automatic expulsion are not proven.
Class C is nominated and the school later confirms a matchup; its predicted academic weakness is not globally quantified.
High–low diagnostic scores follow Horikita's inference and a situational four-band plan; Kōenji cooperation cannot be guaranteed.
School-authorized advance submission is Suzune's independently demonstrated strategy; do not collapse into X's separate messages.
Public apology and classmates' immediate agreement do not create enduring consent or perfect leadership.
Horikita wants to retain Kushida, but the text does not prove Kushida can or must be rehabilitated.
Hirata organizes and supports Horikita's score plan; this is not the exclusive invention of the pairing method.
Hirata's private inference about Kiyotaka as strategist is not certified public knowledge or automatically shared with Ryūen.
Yukimura's three-correct one-partial local quiz is a teaching diagnostic, not an IQ or permanent cognition value.
Keisei is Yukimura's friend-group preferred name, while Teruhiko remains his registered given name; actor ID unchanged.
Yukimura begins tutoring after reflecting on festival limits; no guarantee of unbroken cooperative behavior afterward.
Change in teamwork method does not imply Suzune abandoned her Class A/Manabu objectives.
Horikita's choice not to expel Kushida cannot require Kushida to become trustworthy after the wager.
School question approval is source-backed independent reasoning, not predestination or ownership by X.
Sudō's studied exams incorporate variable difficulty and sports bonuses; training gains can regress.
Yukimura tutoring is a new contextual strategy, not mandatory altruism in all futures.
Preferred given name Keisei cannot rewrite official identity or earlier actor memory.
Sakura joining a circle is an observed initiative, not an automatic romance or universal confidence.
Kiyotaka's friends do not thereby inherit White Room/X information or inevitable future loyalty.
Kushida's retrospective status/approval account is self-report and cannot force identical trauma in divergence.
Conceded bet causes temporary ceasefire while hostility persists, not permanent redemption.
Ryūen suspects X without discovering identity; information goal can evolve without guaranteed coercive tactics.
Ryūen's long-term Class A objective explicitly remains while he tactically sends false Kushida answers.
Ichinose's documented solidarity may persist; tension is not evidence her entire goal was replaced.
Katsuragi's declared regret does not entail a secret anti-Ryūen pact.
Nagumo's presidential policy agenda is a speech, not proof every institutional rule changed.
